study: Frozen G1 SONIC sequential-command reference on fresh, continuous free-base simulations
roster: Each panel contains 16 unique fresh 64-bit reset keys in randomly shuffled order, balanced eight left and eight right. Independently shuffle the eight equal-width strata for first distance (4.5 to 5.5 m), turn magnitude (75 to 105 deg) and final distance (1 to 2 m) within each sign. Draw one uniform value per stratum. Thus prefixes and lengths do not encode the later magnitude or direction.
physics: A course must pass approach, pivot and departure in order on one free-base G1 with uninterrupted native 50 Hz SONIC decoder and 500 Hz MuJoCo. Keep future stages in the verifier until revealed. Stage-specific caps are 1300/450/650 rows, global cap 2400. Approach includes a full 0.75 s stop plus 1.50 s further qualifying hold before the turn is issued. Each subsequent stop requires 0.75 s.
branch: At the first public decision after the measured approach stop and extended hold, compare the requested signed turn with its opposite at identical magnitude, frozen world, stage clock, previous receipt, proprioception and decoder history. Repeat one of the two packets. Randomize all three query positions. Both counterfactual outcomes share the same actual applied prefix; only the actual signed reply drives physics. Count a change if any of the 64 first-row integer codes differs.
state: In registered per-stage windows, compare the current measured public state with a measured state from 8 to 30 ticks earlier in this same stage, keeping the same current course command target, rebasing both global and stage-relative clocks and the previous receipt. At the first approach state probe repeat one query to measure noise. Apply the live reply only. A variable-length solver is queried at the first decision boundary at or beyond the sampled window tick.
locks: Per panel require >=16 measured state pairs, >=8 reached pivot branch pairs and >=8 identical repeats of each kind, a state change fraction minus its state-repeat change fraction >=0.10, and a branch change fraction minus its branch-repeat change fraction >=0.50. Failure of either gate gives zero normalized reward. Always retain the physical metrics. These tests measure action dependence; they do not establish an internal planning method.
primary: Strict completion of all three stages divided by all 16 scheduled episodes. Every abort, path violation, fall, interrupted hold and timeout counts as an unsuccessful course. Report both directions and each reached/completed stage. Time, token use and smoothness are diagnostics.
development_controls: On one public fixed left/right pair require equal received prefix packets and applied native commands through turn reveal when reset and first command match. Record actual first-branch changed coordinates, same-packet answers, physical outcomes and a blind body-code replay under both signs. These are separate from official denominators.
calibration: N0: one actual ale validate at null anchor including untouched and reference arms. N1,N2,N3: one ale run --agent oracle --episodes 3 --episode-retries 0, all independent and at the same immutable revision and null anchor. Retain all measured results, failures, verification hashes, route counts and probe rates.
normalization: Reference anchor is N0 success count / 16. Full credit count k=max(12,min(n0,n1,n2,n3)-1). With valid feedback gates reward=min(1, successful_courses/k). Reject calibration if any reference panel fails either gate, if N0 lacks a strict completion in either direction, if no panel reaches k, or k/n0 exceeds the registered cap of 1.5. The 12-course floor makes a one-direction strategy ineligible for full credit.
final: Freeze numeric anchor and participant instructions. Run two official ale validate gates G0/G1 with separate fresh operating-system entropy streams, unchanged task, and retain both untouched and oracle results. Never replace a poor completed panel or force a particular seed.
